The pipeline begins with the initial measurement input, which is fed into the primary architecture.
An initial residual block processes the measurement input and splits it into two distinct streams.
This initializes both the image state and the auxiliary feature state at step K.
Both states then enter sequential DMP steps to begin the iterative refinement process.
Subsequent DMP steps continue refining both the image and feature
representations across intermediate time steps.
The final DMP step completes the iterative sequence down to step zero.
This yields the fully refined image state and auxiliary feature map at the final step.
A concluding residual block merges the streams to produce the final reconstructed image.
Examining an individual DMP step in detail, the image state and feature state enter as inputs.
The image state passes through a Gradient Descent module to compute an updated signal.
This signal is concatenated channel-wise with the feature state
and routed into a residual block.
The processed output is split channel-wise into an intermediate representation
and the updated feature state.
The intermediate representation enters the conditional probability block
to yield the updated image state.
The detailed ResBlock structure comprises an initial convolution,
four chained residual modules, and a final convolution.
Each individual residual unit contains two convolution layers
with an intermediate ReLU activation and a skip connection.
Finally, the legend defines the symbols for channel splitting, concatenation,
addition, and convolution parameters.
